sections.report:
**Section.** The whole piece: applies.

**Findings**
None.

(For the director, outside this section: the volunteer invitation ("Work days run every second Saturday…", from about y≈406 to 580) is buried in the second half of a single paragraph, with no heading or ask of its own. That belongs to the hierarchy and text critics, not here.)

**What's working.**
- Nothing is extra: there is one heading (about x 180–475, y 120–165) and one paragraph, with no rules, boxes or ornament. Every element earns its place, and the page reads as one piece in one voice.
- The copy is specific and finished. "Eleven miles of footpath", "set up in 1987", "four staff, around ninety volunteers" and "a hot drink at the end" could only be this trust's. A stranger learns exactly who they are and what a work day involves, and there are no placeholders or typos.

**Checklist.** The whole piece: 8 lines, 8 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure.

First read: the eye lands on "About the trust", the bold heading at top left, then drops into one long block of body text. It reads as the About section of a small countryside charity's website. It feels calm and plain, and offers nowhere to stop after the heading.

Job (assumed): tell local visitors what the Moorside Trust is, and invite them to volunteer.

Walk, What matters first:
- One element dominates, so the eye knows where to start: **yes**. The heading (about 40 px, bold, near-black, at x 180–475, y 120–165) is clearly the top of the page.
- Each level of text is distinct, with no near-identical sizes: **yes**. There are two sizes, heading about 40 px and body about 20 px, a 2:1 step.
- Headings also differ in weight, form or color: **yes**. The heading is bold and the body is regular.

Every line is yes, so step 5 is not needed.

**Section.** What matters first: applies.

**Findings**
None.

One point outside the checklist, for the director to weigh: the only thing the reader can act on is in the middle of the paragraph. "Work days run every second Saturday, and anyone is welcome to join for the morning" starts at about y 395, line 7 of 12. It has the same weight as the founding history around it, so a reader skimming for "can I help?" won't find it. This is a sign the piece has only two levels where its content needs three. The fix is to give the volunteer offer its own level, such as a subhead or a separate short paragraph. This is taste, and minor to major depending on whether recruiting volunteers is the page's main job. It probably also falls under arrangement or text (paragraphing).

**What's working.**
- There's one clear step between heading and body: about 2:1 in size plus bold against regular, both in the same near-black. You know immediately where to start, and no in-between size muddies it.
- The heading is set tight, with the body close beneath it (about 30 px gap), so the two read as one unit and the heading clearly owns the text.

**Checklist.** What matters first: 3 lines, 3 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Section.** Arrangement and space: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Is the empty space gathered into a few deliberate areas, rather than left over in scattered small gaps?** and **Does the visual weight balance, with no side, crowded or empty, that makes the page look about to tip?** These two failures come from one problem. All the content sits in one column at x≈180–787, y≈120–582. To its right, x≈790–1280 is empty from top to bottom, about 490 px or 38% of the width. Another ~220 px is empty below the paragraph. The space is gathered into one area, which is good, but nothing shapes it or gives it a job. The text block's centre is at x≈483 against a frame centre of 640, and nothing on the right pushes back. The viewer sees a page that leans left and looks unfinished, as if a sidebar or picture failed to load, rather than a column that chose to stay narrow. Why: Arnheim (*Art and Visual Perception*, "Balance") says an asymmetric layout needs a counterweight on its lighter side. Tschichold and Müller-Brockmann count a large empty area with no reason as a fault. Ruder wants the empty space to stand in tension with the printed area, and here it just sits next to it. Direction of the fix, any one of these:
   - Give the right side something with real weight that belongs to this section, such as a photo of a work day or a short volunteer panel with the Saturday times. Put it on the same grid, top-aligned with the heading at y≈120.
   - Or move the reading column so the space around it looks chosen, for example centred, or with the margins evened out.

   If a picture was meant to fill that space and didn't render, the layout is fine. Check that in a live browser. Convention. Weight: minor. The text still reads well, but the page looks unfinished.

**What's working.**
- The heading and the paragraph share one exact left edge at x≈180. The heading sits ~35 px above the paragraph, close to its line spacing and far tighter than any other gap on the page, so the two clearly read as one group.
- The column is limited to ~600 px, which keeps lines at a comfortable reading length. Keep that width whatever goes on the right.

**Couldn't judge from a still.**
- Whether the empty right side is a picture or panel that didn't load or is hidden at this width, and how the column behaves at narrower and wider viewports.

**Checklist.** Arrangement and space: 13 lines, 11 yes, 2 no (empty space gathered into deliberate areas; visual weight balances)

**Section.** Text: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Is long text broken up by headings, short paragraphs, or lists?** No. The whole section is one paragraph of 12 lines, from about y≈200 to y≈585 at x≈180–786, and it does two different jobs. The first half says what the trust is and where it came from: eleven miles of footpath, set up in 1987, four staff, ninety volunteers, two thousand members. The second half is an invitation: "Work days run every second Saturday, and anyone is welcome to join for the morning. We provide tools, gloves, and a hot drink…". That invitation starts mid-line at about y≈406, after "moor.", so nothing in the layout tells you it is there. A reader who skims sees a grey block of history and leaves before reaching what they could act on: when work days are, that no experience is needed, and that tools are provided. Source: Nielsen, "How Users Read on the Web" (Nielsen Norman Group). The fix is to split the text at "Work days…" into its own short paragraph, or better under its own subhead ("Join a work day"). That puts "every second Saturday" and "no experience needed" where a skimming eye lands. The copy has a related problem: the voice switches from "it" (the trust, in the third person) to "we" at that same point. That switch is one more sign these are two separate pieces of text, and the split would make it read naturally. This is a defect. **Weight: major**, because the call to volunteer is the part most likely to matter to a local reader, and right now it is buried.

**What's working.**
- The measure and leading suit long reading. Body text looks to be about 20 px, with lines of about 55–62 characters at roughly 1.6 line spacing. That is inside Bringhurst's 45–75 range, and the ragged right edge is irregular with no staircase or wedge. Keep this setting when splitting the text.
- There is one family with a clear two-level scale. The heading is a bold display size (about 44 px) and is tracked slightly tighter than the body, so it reads as one solid unit and plainly outranks the regular-weight body. No sizes sit close enough to be mistaken for each other.

**Couldn't judge from a still.** Whether the text is live type rather than a picture of text. Nothing suggests it is a picture, but check it in the browser.

**Checklist.** Text: 30 lines, 29 yes, 1 no (long text broken up by headings, short paragraphs, or lists)

First read: the eye goes to the bold "About the trust" heading at the top left (about x180, y120–165), then down into one long paragraph of near-black text on white. It reads as the About section of a website for a small local charity. It feels plain and quiet, with nothing pulling the eye. Job, assumed: tell local visitors what the trust is and invite them to the work days.

Walk, Color:
- Small palette: yes. White and one near-black, with no hue.
- Strong colour kept to a small share: yes. There is no saturated colour.
- Clear range of light and dark: yes. Dark text on a white field is the full range, and the structure survives grayscale.
- Warm forward, cool back: yes. There are no hues.
- Matching colours look the same: yes. The heading and the body are both near-black and look the same.
- No vibrating edges: yes.
- Status colours used only for their meaning: yes. There are none.
- Meaning not carried by colour alone: yes. Nothing is coded by colour.
- Dark theme background not pure black: yes. It is a light theme.

No line came out `no` or `unsure`, so there are no entries to open.

**Section.** Color: applies. The piece is near-black text on white, with no hue anywhere.

**Findings**
None.

**What's working.** Body and heading text are near-black (about x180–790, y120–580) on a plain white field. That gives the strongest light-to-dark range there is, so the text reads clearly. Both use the same dark tone, so the page doesn't seem to have two colours that almost match. Leaving out colour suits a quiet, informational About page.

**Checklist.** Color: 9 lines, 9 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Section.** Pictures: skipped. The image has no photo, illustration, icon, logo or mark. It holds only a heading ("About the trust") and one paragraph of body text.

**Findings**
None.

**Couldn't judge from a still.** The text block sits in the left part of the frame, from about x 180 to 790. The right side, from about x 800 to 1280 and y 100 to 600, is empty with no placeholder box. This could be a planned single column, or a picture slot that didn't load when the screenshot was taken, such as a photo of the moor or of a work day. I can't tell which from a still. Check the live page for an image that failed to load. If the space is on purpose, it belongs to the arrangement critic, not this section.

**Checklist.** Pictures: skipped

**Section.** Charts and data: skipped. The image is one heading ("About the trust") and a paragraph of prose. It has no chart, table of figures or dashboard. The paragraph does give some figures (eleven miles of footpath, 1987, four staff, about ninety volunteers, just over two thousand members), but they're written as sentences, so they belong to the Text section, not this one.

**Findings**
None.

**Checklist.** Charts and data: skipped
